name: Cinderwake
subtitle: the warm canyons
story: The ground on Cinderwake is warm all year, and so is the rain. At night the canyon walls glow a dull orange, enough to read by. Tea grows wild in the cracks. People leave their kettles out on the rock and come back when they whistle, and socks dry on the walls in about ninety seconds. The only stove on the planet is in a museum, behind a rope.
hook: A planet for people who are always cold.

episode.opener:
The ground here
boils your kettle.

beats.text:
The only stove on the planet
is in a museum, behind a rope.

The oldest law on Cinderwake
is about kettles.

Nobody here is ever cold.
Wilf is.

So, legally, every kettle
on the planet is Wilf's.

At dusk the kettles whistle.
The whole canyon looks round
for Wilf.

He's had tea in every house
on Cinderwake.

episode.caption:
On a warm planet, one man is blowing on his hands.

Cinderwake is big and young and still cooling from the inside, so its heat comes up through the rock, not down from its sun. Towns grew round the hottest stones, the way ours grew round wells. You put a kettle down, wander off, and come back when it whistles. The rain falls warm, tea grows wild in the cracks, and socks dry on the canyon walls in about ninety seconds. Nights last twenty hours, and the canyon walls glow dull orange, enough to read by. The air is thicker than ours, so water boils at about 107°C and visitors burn their tongues. Heating bills are something grandparents mention to frighten children.

I packed a hot-water bottle. It's in the museum now, next to the stove.

Everyone knows a Wilf. Who's yours?

short.title:
The ground here

short.sub:
Nobody is ever cold.

beats.text:
By law, the cold get the kettles.
So every kettle is his.

He's had tea in every house.
No warmer.
